examples.knowledge_point: Finding Partial Derivatives of Three-Variable Functions
examples.problem: For the function  $g(x,y,z) = 2 (x + 1)e^z+ yz,$  evaluate  $\dfrac{\partial g}{\partial z}$ at $(1,1,1).$
examples.worked_solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $z,$ treating all other variables as constants. 

First, we use the sum and constant multiple rules:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(2(x+1){e}^{z}+yz) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(2(x+1){e}^{z})+\frac{∂}{∂z}(yz) \\  & =2(x+1)\frac{∂}{∂z}({e}^{z})+\frac{∂}{∂z}(yz) \\  & =2(x+1){e}^{z}+y\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we evaluate the partial derivative at the point $(1,1,1)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂z}{|}_{(1,1,1)} & =2(1+1){e}^{1}+1 \\  & =4e+1\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Consider the function $f(x,y)=\frac{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}{x-{y}^{2}}.$ The partial derivative of $f$ with respect to $y$ is given by

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂y}=\frac{h(x,y)}{{(x-{y}^{2})}^{2}}.
$$

Find the function $h(x,y).$
feedback.worked_solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $y,$ treating all other variables as constants. 

Using the quotient rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}{x-{y}^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\cdot (x-{y}^{2})-({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(x-{y}^{2})}{{(x-{y}^{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2y\cdot (x-{y}^{2})-({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\cdot (-2y)}{{(x-{y}^{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2xy-2{y}^{3}+2{x}^{2}y+2{y}^{3}}{{(x-{y}^{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2xy+2{x}^{2}y}{{(x-{y}^{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2xy(1+x)}{{(x-{y}^{2})}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
h(x,y)=2xy(1+x).
$$
